title: Greywater and wastewater safety boundaries
summary: Do not improvise wastewater irrigation for edible crops; it requires local rules and risk controls beyond ordinary garden practice.
content: Do not improvise wastewater irrigation for edible crops; it requires local rules and risk controls beyond ordinary garden practice. Use the steps as a conservative offline checklist, then follow current local rules, official alerts, product labels and competent agricultural or food-safety advice.
materials: clean dedicated containers or tools appropriate to the task
steps: Identify the exact source: shower, laundry, kitchen, toilet, sewage, industrial or flood water are not interchangeable.
Check local public-health, plumbing and agricultural rules before designing any reuse system.
Keep untreated sewage, toilet waste, kitchen grease, chemical discharge and floodwater away from food-growing soil.
Where an approved greywater system exists, follow its treatment, subsurface delivery, crop restrictions, monitoring and maintenance requirements.
Switch to a safer water source whenever illness, odour, surfacing water, chemical contamination or system failure is suspected.
warnings: Boiling does not make chemically contaminated water suitable for irrigation or food handling.
Do not use this guide as a design standard for sewage or greywater systems.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.
Using an unidentified material, water source, seed lot or crop.
Ignoring weather, local rules, product labels or signs of contamination.
alternatives: Reduce the plan to one small test batch or container.
Use a safer established water, seed, crop or food method when any critical condition is uncertain.
failure_signs: Unexpected odour, slime, mould, contamination, structural movement, uncontrolled pests, crop collapse or results that contradict the verified method.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this guide to override an emergency order, food recall, pesticide label, building restriction, water restriction or professional diagnosis.
short_term: Protect people, drinking water and uncontaminated food first; isolate the uncertain material and record what happened.
long_term: Keep a seasonal record of materials, varieties, water, weather, yields, losses and corrections.
if_method_fails: Stop scaling up, isolate the problem and return to a verified small trial or qualified local advice.
environment_notes: Adapt for Mediterranean heat, wind, drought, local frost, balcony exposure and the actual microclimate.
